subject: Request: Canary rollout SLAs for latency-sensitive inference
messages:
From: Julie Park <julie.park@optimahealth.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2025-03-11T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Canary rollout SLAs for latency-sensitive inference

Hi Rishi,

We’re preparing a canary/A-B rollout for OptimaHealth’s clinical-triage feature that depends on low-latency LLM inference. Our production SLO is 150ms median, 300ms p95. We want to route ~10% of live traffic to a newly quantized model variant for 72 hours to validate quality and cost.

Before we proceed we need written confirmation from Redwood on two things:
- A temporary SLA carveout/exception for this canary window (we understand carveouts are rare but need clarity on how latency targets and credits apply during the test).
- Mechanisms you will enable by default: automatic fallback to the previous model version if latency or error thresholds are breached, and the ability for OptimaHealth to pin the prior version manually if we detect regressions.

Please let me know the triggers you recommend for an automated fallback (latency p95 threshold? error rate?), whether we can enforce a version pin for the duration of the test, and any specific telemetry or audit logs you will provide for post-mortem.

We’re aiming to start the canary the week of Mar 17. Legal may need an addendum — I’ve CC’d them.

Thanks,
Julie Park
Head of Product Ops
OptimaHealth

Julie — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marcus (serving/runtime) and Grace (CS) so we can align on triggers, telemetry, and an operational playbook. High level: we can support an automated fallback and a model-version pin for the canary window; we just need to agree on thresholds, ramp steps, and the official exception duration to record in our systems.

Proposed next steps:
- Marcus to propose fallback triggers and ramp schedule (2% -> 10% -> 25%) and pin semantics.
- Grace to confirm monitoring dashboards and access (per-route p50/p95, error rate, request volume, sample prompts).
- Rishi to draft a short exception term for legal and include the HubSpot/deal reference.

Could you share the expected traffic distribution during business hours vs off-peak and any golden prompts you want us to evaluate? That will inform thresholds.

We’ll aim to send a technical proposal by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, Julie Park <julie.park@optimahealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2025-03-12T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Canary rollout SLAs for latency-sensitive inference — proposed controls

Thanks for pulling me in. Below is our proposed technical control set that balances your SLO risk while allowing the canary to run:

Automatic fallback triggers (any one will trigger an immediate revert):
- p95 latency breach: p95 > 250ms sustained for a 5-minute window
- Error spike: request error rate > 1.0% in a 1-minute window
- Quality guardrail (optional): degradation on golden prompt set > 3% relative to baseline (we can run automated evals against your provided prompts)

Pin semantics:
- We can enable a model_version_lock flag for your account; once set it prevents auto-roll and pins traffic to the selected version.
- Pin can be applied for a bounded window (we suggest up to 6 hours manually, or 72 hours if you request an exception).

Ramp plan (recommended):
- Step 0: internal dry-run with synthetic traffic
- Step 1: 2% live for 2 hours (monitor p95, errors, sample outputs)
- Step 2: 10% for 24 hours
- Step 3: 25% for 24–48 hours if healthy

Observability we’ll provide:
- Per-route p50/p95/p99 and 1m/5m error rates
- Sampled request/response pairs (redacted) for golden prompt checks
- Real-time alerting (Slack + PagerDuty) on fallback triggers

Attached are a diagram of the fallback flow and a draft pin-config snippet we would apply to your dedicated route. If you’re comfortable with these triggers we’ll bake them into the exception term for legal.

Operational notes:
- During the canary we will record the rollout as an "SLA-exception" ticket in our internal tracker; credits will be evaluated after the window if triggers fired.
- If a fallback occurs we’ll automatically route traffic back to the previous version and keep the canary disabled until a manual restore.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the diagram.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, Julie Park <julie.park@optimahealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, OptimaHealth Legal <legal@optimahealth.com>
Date: 2025-03-13T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Approval: Temporary SLA exception for OptimaHealth canary (conditions)

Julie / team — I’ve reviewed Marcus’s proposed controls and approve a timeboxed SLA exception for the planned canary under the following conditions:

1) Duration and scope: Approved for a 14-day exception window starting on your agreed start date. The exception applies only to the specific route(s) configured for the canary.

2) Triggers & automatic fallback: The fallback triggers Marcus outlined (p95 > 250ms for 5m, error rate >1%/1m, golden-prompt degradation) will be enforced. Any triggered fallback will be treated as a production incident and logged.

3) Pinning and manual locks: OptimaHealth may set a model_version_lock during the window; we’ll honor manual pins up to 72 hours, after which a second approval is required.

4) Monitoring & access: Grace will share dashboard links and alert subscriptions. We require a pre-launch readiness check (infrastructure + synthetic tests) 24 hours before traffic starts.

5) Legal & billing: Legal to sign a short addendum (I’ve attached a draft). Any SLA credits due to a failure in the control logic will be handled per our commercial terms and recorded against deal D-92834.

6) Post-mortem: If a fallback occurs, a joint post-mortem with OptimaHealth must be completed within 72 hours.

Please confirm you accept these conditions and confirm your target start date. Once we have confirmation, Grace and Marcus will schedule the readiness check. I’m copying Legal to start the addendum conversation.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
